stem: Meena sees a shiny object in her classroom and wants to decide if it is a metal. Which statement is not correct?

options.text: Materials with typically shiny surfaces are said to be lustrous.
Any object that looks shiny must be a metal, even if it is only painted or coated.
Metals usually have a lustrous appearance.
A polished wooden surface can shine without being a metal.

teacher.key_rationale: The incorrect statement is B: shine alone is not sufficient evidence that a material is a metal, since polishing, paint or coating can make non-metals appear shiny. A, C and D correctly describe lustre and cautious metal inference.
